text:
Florida scored eight, and the surprising part is that the number was close to fair. The Panthers generated 4.55 expected goals to Seattle's 1.78, and in simulated replays of every shot they win 88 percent of the time. Joey Daccord allowed 3.5 goals more than the 37 shots he faced deserved, while Jacob Markstrom, who allowed three, was beaten by only 1.22 goals' worth of quality.

The game tilted in the first period, when Florida out-chanced Seattle 2.11 to 0.62 in expected goals. Sam Bennett scored 1:05 in, Shane Wright tied it on a tip-in at 4:54, and then Carter Verhaeghe scored at 17:56 and again on the power play at 19:07 to make it 3-1. Matthew Tkachuk assisted on Bennett's opener and the power-play goal, and he finished with three assists. His line's on-ice expected goals were 3.35 for and 0.43 against. The second period turned it into a rout. Verhaeghe completed his hat trick at 6:02, Niko Mikkola scored 40 seconds later, and Bennett made it 6-1 at 13:13.

Seattle did not fold. Frederick Gaudreau scored with 55 seconds left in the second, and Ryker Evans cut it to 7-3 in the third after Sam Reinhart's power-play goal. Bennett added his third at 11:14 to close the scoring. Florida went 2 for 3 with the man advantage, while Seattle was 0 for 4 and won 37 of 56 faceoffs without it mattering. Florida's pressure faded late, with the third period close at 0.83 expected goals to 0.72, but by then the game was long decided.
